comment.narrative: International IDEA and GP hired a consultant to develop a perception survey on the FGM Act targeting parliamentarians political party leaders and other stakeholders. The objectives of the consultancy were to determine the perceptions of parliamentarians political party leaders and other stakeholders on Female Genital Mutilation to identify best practices and to provide recommendations from parliamentarians political party leaders and other stakeholders to strengthen the FGM Act and improve its implementation.Through an online survey 84 responses were collected and analyzed to document the perceptions of those surveyed on the FGM Act.In summary the results of the analysis show that most age groups view the practice as a cultural association. However a small number of individuals in the 2534 age group argue that it has religious roots and significance. This is a significant aspect to consider given the fact that religion is a fundamental part of the lives of Gambians. Notably 88 of the older generation 3444 age group also see the practice as both religious and cultural. While both genders may acknowledge FGM as a cultural practice a significant portion of women 89 endorse this cultural and religious justification. This suggests a need to explore the gendered perspectives on FGM in greater depth with regard to the perception of it as a cultural or religious practice. In conclusion the respondents recommended working with practicing communities to develop alternative rites of passage ARPs as a way to support the cultural value of the practice while simultaneously eliminating its harmful aspects and consider establishing a committee at the National Assembly focused on enforcing and monitoring compliance with the FGM ban law.
